title: Customer topology replay compiler for on‑prem benchmarking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a compiler that converts a compact customer environment description (topology, route mix, model versions, hardware profile, network characteristics, and token-level request traces if available) into reproducible load jobs for on-prem / VPC benchmarking. The goal is to run deterministic, debuggable, and parametrizable experiments that: 1) reproduce customer-like token/sec profiles, 2) surface p95 latency regressions between runtime versions or quantization profiles, and 3) produce artifacts usable for root-cause analysis (per-request traces, kernel selection logs, and KV-cache warmup graphs). This ticket focuses on the compiler and canonical job format; the runner integration and dashboarding are separate follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact YAML/JSON schema (compiler input) that models: routes, traffic mix, model variants, per-route QPS and token distribution, cold/warm start percentages, and optional recorded request traces.

Implement a compiler binary/service that emits a validated, versioned job payload consumable by the existing replay runner with options: deterministic seed, max-requests, duration, and token-rate-smoothing parameters.
Compiler supports network perturbations (latency jitter, packet loss) as emulation hooks to simulate noisy customer networks for on-prem runs.
End-to-end run of a compiled job reproduces a previously captured customer p95 within +/-10% on a matched hardware profile (documented reproduction test).
Generated artifacts: per-request latency histogram, token/sec timeline, p95 delta report vs baseline, and a zipped trace bundle uploaded to S3/ARTIFACTS for troubleshooting.
Unit tests and an integration smoke test that runs a 30s job on CI (using a tiny synthetic topology) and validates schema round-trip and artifact generation.
Documentation: spec page in Confluence with example descriptors and a short runbook for on-call to interpret the artifacts.
Security: compiler input validation and no secret leakage; security review completed and signed off.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: schema design and reference compiler (Go). Deliver a minimal schema that captures route-level distributions and a compact representation for recorded traces (token length, model-id, time offsets). Phase 2: compile-to-runner adapter that produces runner-compatible jobs and a small shim that injects KV-cache warmup and controlled cold-starts. Phase 3: add network emulation hooks and deterministic-seed support, plus automated artifact upload to ARTIFACTS. Phase 4: integrate with perf dashboards and add a regression detection job that automatically compares new runs to an archived baseline and flags regressions above configurable thresholds.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Initial spike complete. Drafted schema with fields for routes, token-level histograms, model_version, hardware_profile, and network_emulation. Chose YAML for human readability and versioned via 'compiler_schema_v1'.

2026-03-12 Marco Liu: Observed p95 skew when running quantized model variant in on-prem staging: ~12% higher than baseline; artifact bundle created (s3://artifacts/redwood/perf/ENG-30012/2026-03-12). Created follow-up ticket for kernel selection investigation.

2026-03-13 Aisha Patel: Added network jitter parameter and a 'warmup_steps' option so KV-cache prefetch can be toggled per job. Pushed branch compiler/ENG-30012 with tests. Opened PR #4892 for review.
notes: Design decisions: 1) Use YAML input for readability and to encourage engineering/SE adoption; 2) Compiler outputs runner JSON to avoid changing runner API; 3) Deterministic seed + recorded traces enables exact replay for short windows; longer runs will use statistical matching of token-length distribution and inter-arrival times. Open questions: how to version baselines reliably across hardware drift; whether to include a lightweight simulator for kernel scheduling to triage without dedicated GPUs. Follow-ups: add a canary job that runs compiled customer topologies nightly against dedicated staging capacity and posts regression alerts to #perf-alerts.
